lesson.scenario: A per-tenant limiter admits five requests in each wall-clock-aligned 60-second window.
entities: Issues requests around a minute boundary
Stores the active window id and count
Increments only when count is below five

steps.title: Window 120 opens
steps.narration: The first request at second 7201 selects minute window 120 and creates its counter.
steps.outcome: A fresh key isolates this minute from the preceding window.
steps.invariant: All requests with window id 120 contend on the same atomic counter.

steps.title: First three admitted
steps.narration: Three requests atomically increment the active counter from zero to three.
steps.outcome: Two admissions remain in the current fixed interval.
steps.invariant: The count and admission decision are one atomic operation.

steps.title: Quota is consumed
steps.narration: Requests four and five advance the counter exactly to its limit.
steps.outcome: Five requests have been admitted in window 120.
steps.invariant: An admitted count may equal but never exceed the configured limit.

steps.title: Same-window excess rejected
steps.narration: A sixth request at 7259 sees count five and does not mutate it.
steps.outcome: The old window remains capped at five.
steps.invariant: Rejected requests do not consume quota unless that policy is explicitly chosen.

steps.title: Boundary creates new quota
steps.narration: At second 7260 the next request maps to window 121 and increments a different counter.
steps.outcome: Quota resets abruptly at the aligned boundary.
steps.invariant: Fixed windows can admit up to twice the nominal limit across two adjacent boundary instants.

production.scenario: A consumer identity service limits password reset emails per source IP in five-minute billing windows during a credential-stuffing wave.
components: submits password reset requests from home and mobile networks
owns reset initiation for the identity edge
publishes the current per-IP fixed-window caps
admits or rejects each reset request for the active window
authoritative sink for reset jobs delivered to the mailer
stores active limiter shard checkpoints for rollouts
stores rejected reset evidence for automated investigation
flows: A user asks for a reset link while attackers are probing the same network range.
The API fetches the five-minute per-IP threshold for the current tenant and region.
The limiter receives the current fixed-window contract before evaluating the call.
The API binds the request to the current billing window instead of an exact trailing interval.
Admitted requests become durable mail jobs that downstream mailers can retry independently.
Checkpoint metadata is written so a rolling restart keeps the same window owner.
Rejected calls are preserved for abuse automation and operator review.
